• Third Report: The Messenger ﷺ would raise his hands at the opening takbir, then would not raise them again (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 224).

f: What statement does 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ make in his fourth report regarding the early Caliphs?
b: "I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, and 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ. They did not raise their hands except at the beginning of prayer" (Nasb al-raya 1:526, Majma' al-zawa'id 2:101).

f: What do the narrations of Salim from his father (Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا) (such as in Sahih Ibn 'Awana 2:90 U) confirm regarding hand-raising?
b: Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا stated that when beginning prayer, the Messenger ﷺ would raise his hands to shoulder level and thereafter would not raise them again before or after bowing, nor between the two prostrations (sujud). This confirms the Messenger ﷺ did not raise his hands at the time of ruku', a report also transmitted by Imam Humaydi in his Musnad via a rigorous chain.

f: What do 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا report regarding seven instances where hands are to be raised (Nasb al-raya 1:521)?
b: The hands are to be raised at: (1) the beginning of prayer, (2) when setting sight on the House of Allah, (3) at Safa, (4) Marwa, (5) 'Arafat, (6) Muzdalifa, and (7) when saluting the [black] stone. Notably, there is no mention of raising hands at the time of bowing (ruku').

f: What is narrated by Jabir ibn Samura رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ regarding the prohibition of raising hands, and how do Hanafis interpret it?
b:
• Narration: The Messenger ﷺ approached and remarked, "Why is it that I see you raising your hands as though they are the tails of restive horses? Remain calm in prayer" (Sahih Muslim 1:181, Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:176, Sunan Abi Dawud 1:150).

• Interpretation: The Prophet ﷺ prohibited raising hands while performing prayer (during ruku', prostration, etc.). This cannot apply to the opening takbir, since raising hands then is outside the formal actions of prayer (tahrima) and does not interfere with the prescribed calmness (sukoon).

f: How do scholars distinguish Jabir ibn Samura's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narration about "tails of restive horses" from the separate narration concerning salam?
b:
Some mistakenly claim the hadith refers to making salam at the end of prayer. However, comparing the circumstances proves they are two separate incidents:

1. In Jabir's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narration, Companions were engrossed in prayer when addressed, whereas the salam narration involves gesturing when making salam.

2. Jabir's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narration prohibits "raising hands during prayer" and instructs calmness in prayer, whereas the salam narration prohibits gesturing right and left with hands when making salam.

3. The wording explicitly uses "in prayer," whereas salam is made at the conclusion of prayer.

f: What do the two narrations of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas ؓ (reports 9 and 10) state regarding hand placement outside of prayer?
b: The hands should not be raised except at seven instances: at the beginning of prayer, when entering Masjid al-Haram and setting sight on the House of Allah, when standing on Safa, Marwa, 'Arafat, Muzdalifa, and (in report 10) when pelting the jamarat (Nasb al-raya 1:290 U, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237).

f: What does Bara' ibn 'Azib ؓ report regarding the Messenger's ﷺ hand-raising in prayer (reports 11 and 12)?
b:
• Ibn Abi Layla report: Observed the Messenger ﷺ raise his hands at the initial takbir when beginning prayer (Daraqutni 1:293), and Ibn Abi Layla himself was known not to raise his hands thereafter (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237). 

• Bara' ibn 'Azib report: When the Messenger ﷺ would begin prayer, he would raise his hands up to his ears, then not do so again. One version adds "only once," and another adds "then he would not raise them again until completing the prayer" (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236, Sunan Abi Dawud 1:109 U).

f: What do the reports from Aswad, 'Abd al-Malik, 'Asim ibn Kulayb (from 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ), and Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ state regarding Companions and Followers?
b:
• Aswad: Performed prayer with 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and observed him raise his hands only when beginning prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237). 

• 'Abd al-Malik: Observed that Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, and Abu Ishaq did not raise their hands except at the beginning of prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:237). 

• 'Asim ibn Kulayb (from his father, companion of 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ): 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ would raise his hands only at the initial takbir when beginning prayer; thereafter, he would not raise them again at any other place (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ 94, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236). 

• Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ would raise his hands at the beginning of prayer, then would not raise them again (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236).

f: What do the reports from Mujahid, Imam Malik (via Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ), and Abu Ishaq state?
b:
• Mujahid: Did not see 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ raise his hands except at the beginning of prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236). 

• Imam Malik (from Na'im ibn 'Abdallah al-Mujmir and Abu Ja'far al-Qari): Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ would lead them in prayer, saying the takbir every time he moved from one posture to another, but would raise his hands when saying the takbir at the beginning of the prayer [only] (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ 90). 

• Abu Ishaq: The companions of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ would not raise their hands except at the beginning of prayer; Waki' confirms they would not raise them thereafter (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 1:236).

f: What conclusion is drawn from the list of Companions and Followers who did not raise their hands?
b: Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, and many other Companions, followed by Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Abu Ishaq, Qays, Aswad, 'Alqama, and Ibn Abi Layla, all did not raise their hands except at the initial takbir. They would not have omitted raising hands at ruku' had it been the regular practice of the Messenger ﷺ.

f: How do Qur'anic verses on khushu' (humility) and qunut (devoutness) (2:2; 2:238) relate to the reasoning for not raising the hands?
b:
• 2:3:2: "Successful indeed are the believers, those who humble themselves [khashi'un] in their prayers". 

• 2:2:238: "Stand before Allah in a devout frame of mind [qanitin]". 

Both humility (khushu') and calmness are required in salat. Because the Prophet ﷺ prohibited raising hands due to interference with calmness (resembling tails of restive horses), not raising the hands maintains this prescribed stillness and devout frame of mind.

f: How do Hanafi scholars apply the principle of naskh (abrogation) to the issue of raising hands at ruku'?
b: Whenever naskh occurred regarding a prayer action, it always concerned an action that was initially commanded and practiced, since nonexistent practices cannot be abrogated (just as early talking/moving in prayer were initially permitted and later abrogated). Thus, raising hands at ruku' was initially allowed and later abrogated, leaving only the opening takbir. Furthermore, hadiths prohibiting raising hands (e.g., Jabir ibn Samura's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narration) are consistent and preferred over inconsistent ones, and narrators who report hand-raising (like Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا) have themselves been reported not to raise their hands, whereas the primary narrator of non-raising, Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, never deviated from his consistent reports.

f: What points are made regarding the juristic rank (fiqh) and age/proximity of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ؓ compared to Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا?
b:
• Juristic Rank: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud was a greater jurist than Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, and Ibn Mas'ud's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ students ('Alqama and Aswad) were greater jurists than Nafi' (who reported from Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا); hence, by usul al-hadith, Ibn Mas'ud's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ narrations are preferred. 

• Age & Proximity: Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was older than Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, giving him more opportunity to stand in the first row closer to the Messenger ﷺ for a clearer view, whereas Ibn 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا youth meant he did not stand in the front rows. Moreover, Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ enjoyed an exceptionally close relationship as a personal servant and teacher of the Qur'an who was extremely scrupulous in his narrations.

f: What incidents are related by Mughira ibn Muqsim and Urwa ibn Murra regarding Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and 'Alqama ibn Wa'il?
b:
• Mughira ibn Muqsim: Mentioned Wa'il ibn Hujr's hadith of raising hands to Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, who responded: "If Wa'il has seen the Messenger ﷺ raising his hands once, then Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ has seen him fifty times not raising them" (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar). 

• Urwa ibn Murra: Entering the mosque of Hadhramaut, he heard 'Alqama ibn Wa'il narrate hand-raising from his father. When mentioning this to Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Ibrahim عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ responded angrily: "Is Wa'il ibn Hujr the only one to have seen the Messenger ﷺ? Did not Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and his companions also see him?" (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ 92).

f: How does the presence of physical body motions in prayer support the allocation of hand-raising to the opening takbir?
b: All other invocations in prayer are accompanied by a specific body motion (e.g., takbir before bowing, tasmi' when returning, takbir before prostration). Since there is no accompanying body motion for the beginning and ending of prayer, raising hands was allocated to the opening takbir (and turning the head for taslim). If hands were raised at ruku', the takbir and tasmi' would be accompanied by two actions (bowing down and raising hands), violating the standard of having only one motion per invocation.

f: What is the chapter's final conclusion regarding raf' al-yadayn before and after bowing?
b: Hadiths mentioning hand-raising at ruku' do not establish it as a permanent practice (sunna mustamirra); rather, raising hands before and after bowing is a sunna matruka ("an earlier practice of Allah's Messenger ﷺ which he later abandoned"). Hanafis acknowledge the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands at various instances, but as a temporary practice, with regular raising restricted to the opening takbir (while a weak/fabricated narration of Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا claiming lifelong practice contains fabricators like 'Isma ibn Muhammad and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Quraysh).

f: What are the definitions and physical descriptions of the tawarruk and iftirash sitting postures in prayer?
b:
• Tawarruk: When a person sits with the left posterior on the ground; his right foot placed vertically with toes pointing towards the qibla; and the left foot on its side emerging from under the right foot. 

• Iftirash: Placing the left foot on its side and sitting on it; and keeping the right foot vertical, while resting on the bottom of the toes, turning them toward the qibla.

f: What are the four different group opinions regarding when to use iftirash versus tawarruk in the sittings of prayer?
b:
1. Hanafi view: The more superior and preferred method is to use iftirash in all sittings of the prayer, though sitting in tawarruk is also permissible based on sahih hadiths. 

2. Second group: More preferable to use tawarruk in all sittings of the prayer. 

3. Third group: More preferable to use iftirash in the first sitting and tawarruk in the "final" one (meaning a 2-rak'a prayer uses tawarruk for its only sitting). 

4. Fourth group: Use iftirash in the "first" sitting of every prayer and tawarruk in the second (so a 2-rak'a prayer uses iftirash, while 3 or 4-rak'a prayers use iftirash for the first sitting and tawarruk for the second sitting).

f: How does the Hanafi school explain the occasions when the Messenger ﷺ used tawarruk?
b: The Hanafis state the Prophet ﷺ sat in iftirash for the greater part of his life in all sittings. The few times he did tawarruk was either due to physical weakness/age making it difficult to sit in iftirash in the latter part of his life, or merely to inform the Companions of its permissibility (bayanan li 'l-jawaz).

f: What do the narrations from 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Sahih Muslim, Sahih al-Bukhari, Sunan al-Nasa'i) state regarding iftirash?
b:
• 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spread his left foot and keep the right one standing" (Sahih Muslim 1:195). 

• 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: "It is a sunna of prayer that you keep your right foot standing and fold the left one" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:114); and "among the sunnats of prayer is that you keep the right foot standing with the toes pointed towards the qibla, and [that you] sit on the left foot" (Sunan al-Nasa'i 1:173). 

• Wa'il ibn Hujr ؓ: "I came to Madina to observe the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ prayer. When he sat for tashahhud, he spread his left foot and kept the right one standing" (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:65, classified as sahih and noted by Tirmidhi as the practice of the majority, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, and the people of Kufa).

f: How do scholars reason that iftirash entails more reward based on difficulty, quoting 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا?
b: Iftirash is slightly more difficult than tawarruk, and the more difficult a form of worship, the more reward it entails. As 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا relates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The reward is in proportion to the hardship [you undertake]" (Sahih al-Bukhari, Muslim).

f: How do Hanafis and scholars respond to narrations describing the Messenger ﷺ or companions sitting in tawarruk or cross-legged (tarabbu' SY)?
b:
1. Weakness/Age: The Prophet ﷺ or Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا adopted tawarruk or cross-legged sitting due to physical weakness, pain, or difficulty in their legs/advanced age during their final years, as confirmed by Ibn 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا statement ("My legs do not support me") (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar, Sahih al-Bukhari). 

2. Permissibility (Bayanan li 'l-jawaz): Used on rare occasions simply to demonstrate that sitting in tawarruk or cross-legged is permissible and not unlawful. 

3. Action vs. Verbal Command (Hadith Fi'li vs. Qawli): Tawarruk narrations describe an action (hadith fi'li), whereas iftirash is supported by explicit verbal commands (ahadith qawliyya), which take precedence in usul al-hadith. 

4. Reconciliation: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi narrated both postures because his later narration highlighted the Prophet's ﷺ practice in his final years due to weakness, while his general/earlier narrations establish iftirash as the regular, continuous practice.

f: What is the final conclusion of the chapter regarding the sitting postures in prayer?
b: Both iftirash and tawarruk are found in the hadith literature and both are permissible, so a person has the choice of sitting in either position. However, because the Messenger ﷺ used iftirash for most of his life and as his continuous practice (confirmed by Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا), sitting in iftirash is more virtuous and rewarding, while recourse to tawarruk is made in the event of inability or weakness.

f: What importance and virtues are attributed to the sunna prayer of Fajr in the hadiths of 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا and Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ?
b:
• 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا (Sahih Muslim 1:251): The Prophet ﷺ was more regular and hastened towards the two rak'ats before Fajr than any other supererogatory (nafl) prayer, stating: "They are more superior than the world and everything within it" / "They are more beloved to me than the entire world". 

• Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sunan Abi Dawud 1:186, Athar al-sunan 1:224): "Do not abandon the sunna rak'ats of Fajr, even if horses trample over you".

f: What is the general rule regarding performing sunna prayers once the iqama has been called (Sahih Muslim 1:247)?
b: The Messenger ﷺ stated: "Once the call to commence [iqama] is made for the prayer, there is no prayer except the fard prayer [maktuba]". Thus, once congregational fard prayer begins, no other sunna prayer is permissible in other prayers.

f: What is the dilemma when a person arrives late for Fajr and finds the congregational prayer about to begin or in progress, and what are the differing opinions?
b:
• Dilemma: Balancing the extreme emphasis on the Fajr sunna against the rule prohibiting sunna prayers once iqama or fard begins. 

• Opinion 1: Immediately join the congregation for fard, as performing sunna during congregational fard is no longer permissible (ruling for other prayers). 

• Imam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ & Imam Malik: Attempt to perform the sunna prayer if confident of completing it quickly and joining the fard before it ends (even if catching only the last sitting), provided one is confident of not missing the congregation completely; otherwise, abandon sunna and join the congregation. 

• Additional Hanafi View: Only attempt the sunna if confident of acquiring at least one rak'a behind the imam (certain of catching him before he stands up from ruku' of the second rak'a of fard). 

(Note: If performed after the fard prayer has begun, the Fajr sunna should be done outside the main prayer-hall/masjid area where the congregation is in progress).

f: What do the reports from Nafi', Abu Ishaq, Abu 'Uthman al-Ansari, and Imam Tahawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (regarding Abu 'l-Darda') state about Companions performing the Fajr sunna when joining late?
b:
• Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (via Nafi'): Awakened when prayer had commenced, he arose and performed the two rak'ats (sunna first) (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:375).

• 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: Arriving when congregation had begun, he positioned himself behind a pillar in the masjid and performed two rak'ats sunna first, then joined the congregation (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:374).

• 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas: Arrived while the imam was leading Fajr; since he had not yet performed the two rak'ats sunna, he performed them behind the imam (separately), then joined the congregation (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:375).

• Abu 'l-Darda': Would enter the masjid while everybody was in rows performing Fajr, perform his two rak'ats in a corner of the masjid, then join the fard prayer (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:375).

f: What do the reports from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, Haritha ibn Mudrib, Abu 'l-Darda', Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, Sha'bi (regarding Masruq), and Hasan al-Basri state?
b:
• 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (via Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi): When congregation had already started, they would first perform their two rak'ats at the rear of the masjid, then join the congregation (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:376).

• Haritha ibn Mudrib: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abu Musa رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ left Sa'id ibn al-'As; congregation had begun, so Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ performed two rak'ats sunna first, while Abu Musa رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ joined the row immediately (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:251).

• Abu 'l-Darda': If he entered and found everyone in prayer, he would go to a pillar and perform two rak'ats quickly, then join the congregation (Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 1:443; also noted in another report).

• Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: Sometimes joined immediately, and at other times would first perform his two rak'ats at one side of the masjid (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:251).

• Masruq (via Sha'bi): Entered to find people in Fajr prayer; since he had not performed the two rak'ats sunna, he performed them at one side, then joined the congregation (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:251, Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 2:444).

• Hasan al-Basri: Instructed that when you enter the masjid and find the imam in prayer and have not yet performed the two rak'ats of Fajr, perform them first, then join the imam in the fard prayer (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:445, Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:376).

f: What are the four reasons / arguments provided in support of the Hanafi opinion regarding performing the Fajr sunna late?
b:
1. Greater Emphasis: The emphasis on the sunna of Fajr is far greater than any other sunna prayer (ordered to be performed even if horses trample over the person), excluding it from the general prohibition once congregation begins.

2. Lengthy Recitation in Fajr: Fajr fard involves a lengthy recitation of the Qur'an, making it feasible to quickly perform the two rak'ats sunna and still join the imam during the first rak'a, second rak'a, or just before the salam (unlike other prayers with shorter recitations and four rak'ats).

3. Non-General Command: The command prohibiting non-fard prayers when congregation begins is not an absolute general command encompassing all situations (analogous to how scholars permit performing sunna prayers at home even after knowing congregation has begun in the masjid).

4. Meaning of "Maktuba": The word maktuba in the hadith includes missed (qada') prayers, indicating missed prayers can be performed even after congregation has begun; thus the command is not taken literally in an absolute sense.

f: What are the three main issues regarding witr prayer that the chapter focuses on?
b: (1) How many rak'ats is the witr prayer? (2) How many salams in the witr prayer? (3) Is performing one rak'a sufficient for witr?

f: What are the varying opinions of the schools regarding the number of rak'ats and structure of witr?
b:
• Imam Shafi'i: Witr can be performed in units of one, three, five, seven, nine, or eleven rak'ats. (Though some Shafi'is differentiate between Ramadan vs. other months, or congregation vs. individual).

• Imam Ahmad: Odd rak'ats ranging from one to eleven; main view is performing witr as one rak'a preceded by qiyam al-layl.

• Imam Malik: Recommends at least three rak'ats; does not recommend a single rak'a for witr.

• Imam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: Witr should be performed as three continuous rak'ats with two sittings (one in the second rak'a and the other in the third) with salams to be performed in the final sitting only.

f: What did 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا report regarding the Prophet's ﷺ night and witr prayer (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim)?
b:
• The Prophet ﷺ would not perform more than eleven rak'ats (neither in Ramadan nor out of it): performing four rak'ats (of great beauty and length), followed by another four, and then performing three [witr].

• When asked if he slept before performing witr, he replied: "O 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا! My eyes sleep, but my heart does not".

f: What does Sa'id ibn Hisham relate from 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا regarding the structure of the three rak'ats of witr (Sunan al-Nasa'i, Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ)?
b: 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not make salams in the second rak'a of witr.

f: What do the narrations of Imam Hakim (al-Mustadrak 1:304) and Sa'id ibn Hisham state regarding making salams in witr?
b:
• Imam Hakim / 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not make salams in the first two rak'ats of witr (al-Mustadrak 1:304); he would perform three rak'ats of witr making salams only at the end (in the final rak'a), which was also the practice of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and the people of Madina. 

• Sa'id ibn Hisham (Musnad Ahmad 6:156 U): After 'Isha, the Prophet ﷺ would perform sets of two rak'ats, and thereafter perform the witr prayer without any interval in between (i.e., without salams in the second rak'a).

f: How do scholars explain narrations mentioning numbers like "four with three, six with three, or eight with three" (Sunan Abi Dawud 1:200)?
b: The whole tahajjud prayer has been described as witr, whereas in reality only three rak'ats were witr, and the remaining four, six, or eight rak'ats were tahajjud. Umm al-mu'minin 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا distinguished between the three rak'ats of witr and the various other rak'ats.

f: What surahs did the Prophet ﷺ recite in the three rak'ats of witr according to 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا and Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Sunan Abi Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, etc.)?
b:
• First rak'a: Sabbih isma rabbika al-a'la [Surat al-A'la]. 

• Second rak'a: Qul ya ayyuha 'l-kafirun [Surat al-Kafirun]. 

• Third rak'a: Qul huwallahu ahad [Surat al-Ikhlas] along with the Mu'awwadhatayn [Surat al-Falaq and al-Nas]. (Declared sound [hasan] by Imam Tirmidhi, and authenticated by Imam Hakim and 'Allama Dhahabi).

f: Which other Companions are listed as narrating or supporting that witr consists of three rak'ats concluded with salams only at the end?
b: (1) 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, (2) Ubay ibn Ka'b, (3) 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, (4) 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, (5) 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, (6) Nu'man ibn Bashir, (7) Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, (8) 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, (9) 'Imran ibn Husayn, (10) Abu Khaythama (via his father Mu'awiya ibn Khadij), and (11) Anas ibn Malik رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (via Thabit al-Bunani, noting it was acquired from Jibril عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ from Allah).

f: What reports from Miswar ibn Makhrama, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Hasan al-Basri, and 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud confirm the practice of three rak'ats with one set of salams?
b:
• Miswar ibn Makhrama: After burying Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ remembered he hadn't performed witr; he led them in three rak'ats and made salams only at the end in the third rak'a (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:293 U). 

• 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: Stated he would not neglect the three rak'ats of witr even for red camels (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ 150), and performed them without intermediate salams (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:295). 

• Hasan al-Basri: Informed that 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ practice was to stand up for the third without making salams after the second, noted 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was a greater jurist (al-Mustadrak 1:304). 

• 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: Stated the rak'ats of witr are three, similar to the daytime witr prayer (i.e., Maghrib) (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ 150), and explicitly stated that one rak'a does not suffice for witr (Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ 150).

f: What do the reports from Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, Ubay ibn Ka'b, Abu Umama, and others state concerning the number of rak'ats in witr?
b:
• Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:293): Witr is three rak'ats. 

• Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (via Abu Mansur and 'Ata'): Stated witr is three rak'ats and is similar to the Maghrib prayer (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar, Muwatta Imam Muhammad رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ 150). 

• Ubay ibn Ka'b (via Hasan al-Basri): Would perform three rak'ats for witr and would make salams only at the end of the third rak'a (Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq 2:294). 

• Abu Umama (via Abu Ghalib): Would perform three rak'ats for witr (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294). 

• Alqama: Stated witr is three rak'ats (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294). 

• Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: Stated there is no witr consisting of less than three rak'ats (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294). 

• Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: Designated the rak'ats of witr to be three based on the ruling of the jurists, with salams to be made only at the end (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar). 

• Hasan al-Basri: Stated that the Muslims have reached a consensus (ijma') concerning witr being three rak'ats with salams only at the end (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:294).

f: What is the consensus among the prominent Companions, Followers, and the Fuqaha' Sab'a regarding witr?
b: Prominent Companions like 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, Ubay ibn Ka'b, and Abu Umama all stated in clear terms that witr consists of three rak'ats. Subsequent Followers (Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay, 'Alqama, Abu Ishaq, Qasim ibn Muhammad) and the fuqaha' sab'a ("the seven great jurists") also concluded that witr was three rak'ats, leading Hasan al-Basri to report consensus (ijma') on this.

f: What are the two differing opinions regarding the number of salams in the witr prayer?
b:
1. Hanafi Opinion: Like every other prayer, only one set of salams should be made in witr, concluding at the end of the third rak'a without performing two sets of salams that would perform the third rak'a separately. 

2. Other Scholars' Opinion: The person praying (musalli) should first perform two rak'ats, terminate them with salams, and then perform the third rak'a separately with another set of salams.

f: How do Hanafis answer narrations stating that witr was performed as a single rak'a (such as those attributed to Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا)?
b:
• Many scholars claim that Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا never actually saw the Messenger ﷺ perform the witr prayer, and his narrations cannot be preferred over those of 'Aisha and Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, both of whom were known to have seen the Prophet ﷺ perform it. 

• The Messenger ﷺ prohibited the "incomplete prayer" (butayra), where a person performs a single rak'a as witr. Although this narration has minor weaknesses, its prohibition holds due to being authenticated through reliable chains (asnad); Hafiz Ibn Hajar related it through a strong chain in Lisan al-Mizan, and Hakim al-Naysaburi called it authentic. Thus, the prohibition of performing one rak'a separately stands as a strong command.

f: How do scholars address the narration comparing witr to Maghrib, and the report prohibiting witr to be performed like Maghrib?
b:
• Comparison to Maghrib: Just as Maghrib contains only one set of salams at the end, "the witr prayer of the night" should also be offered like Maghrib—with only one set of salams in the last rak'a. 

• Prohibition report: The report stating the Prophet ﷺ prohibited witr from being performed like Maghrib actually means one should not perform witr alone, like Maghrib, without performing any dual sets of rak'ats (shuf'a) before it; it does not mean one must make salams in between and separate the last rak'a from the first two.

f: What role did the Fuqaha' Sab'a ("the seven great jurists") and Hasan al-Basri play regarding the structure of witr?
b:
• The Seven Jurists: All agreed that witr was to be performed as three rak'ats with salams made only in the last rak'a. These jurists (Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, Qasim ibn Muhammad, Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, Kharija ibn Zayd, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, and Sulayman ibn Yasar عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ) were consulted for legal rulings (fatwa). 

• Hasan al-Basri: Reported a consensus (ijma') on the opinion that witr was three continuous rak'ats without intervals, which was widely accepted among Companions and Followers.

f: How do scholars reconcile Sa'id ibn Hisham's narration from 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا regarding the 9 or 7 rak'ats (Sahih Muslim 1:256)?
b:
• The transmissions show that the Prophet ﷺ would perform up to eleven rak'ats at night, including witr and succeeding rak'ats. 

• Out of those, three rak'ats were witr, and he would sit in the second rak'a of witr without making any salams, performing the final rak'a and concluding with salams at the end. 

• The apparent confusion arises because 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا was specifically asked about the witr prayer details and mentioned the total night vigil (tahajjud) counts together, but other collections (Sunan al-Nasa'i, Muwatta Imam Malik, Musnad Ahmad) clarify that he performed three rak'ats of witr without any interval/salams in between.

f: How do scholars interpret 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narration stating "thirteen rak'ats, five of which would be witr" (Sahih Muslim)?
b:
• The apparent wording might suggest a continuous set of five rak'ats, but this is not taken literally. 

• 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا was specifying the total number of rak'ats performed at night and included in that count the two rak'ats of nafl performed sitting down after the three rak'ats of witr. Thus, "five of which would be witr" means the three rak'ats of witr plus the two succeeding nafl rak'ats.

f: How is the statement "he would sit only at the end" in 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narration interpreted by scholars vs. Hanafis?
b:
• General Interpretation: It means he would not sit for any lengthy period of time for extra du'a and dhikr except at the very end; he sat briefly in every other rak'a to recite tashahhud. The final sitting refers to the final sitting of his two rak'ats nafl salat that followed witr. 

• Hanafi Interpretation: Since tahajjud was performed standing or sitting down and witr standing up, the two rak'ats following witr were performed sitting down. Thus, after performing the first eleven or so rak'ats standing, the Prophet ﷺ sat down to perform the last two rak'ats of nafl sitting down.

f: How do scholars (including Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani) interpret the narration "when one anticipates the break of dawn, he should perform one more rak'a which will convert what he has performed into witr" (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim)?
b:
• This is not taken literally to mean a single isolated rak'a is performed on its own. 

• As Hafiz Ibn Hajar explains in Fath al-Bari (2:385 U), a person performs tahajjud in sets of two throughout the night, and upon reaching the end of his vigil (qiyam al-layl), he should add an extra rak'a to the final set of two and make it three rak'ats. 

• This makes the tahajjud and witr add up to an odd number in accordance with the Prophet's ﷺ statement. Just as the hadith on pilgrimage ("The Pilgrimage is 'Arafat") highlights the primary integral (wuquf) without ignoring other requirements, stating witr is "one rak'a" defines the distinctive factor of adding an extra rak'a to the last two rak'ats of tahajjud to turn them into three rak'ats of witr.

f: How do scholars (such as Ishaq ibn Ibrahim Rahway and Imam Abu Muhammad al-Manbaji) explain narrations that mention numbers like thirteen rak'ats of witr?
b:
• Ishaq ibn Ibrahim Rahway (quoted by Tirmidhi): Performing thirteen rak'ats actually means performing thirteen rak'ats including the three rak'ats of witr, such that the whole night prayer was referred to as witr. 

• Imam Abu Muhammad al-Manbaji: Reconciles the conflicting narrations by explaining that initially the Messenger ﷺ used to perform one rak'a as witr and instructed others in it, but his final and settled practice was to perform three rak'ats.

f: What is the final conclusion of the chapter regarding the performance of the witr prayer?
b:
• Witr should be performed as a three-rak'a prayer, as that is how the majority of narrations state the Messenger ﷺ performed it. 

• These three rak'ats should be performed together without separating the third rak'a from the first two (with only one set of salams at the end of the third rak'a, just like the Maghrib prayer). 

• Performing one rak'a independently has been classified as an incomplete prayer (butayra).

f: What are the different scholarly opinions regarding performing tahiyyat al-masjid, nafl, or making up missed prayers after 'Asr?
b:
• Imam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: It is not permissible for a musalli to perform tahiyyat al-masjid (two rak'ats upon entering the masjid) or any other supererogatory (nafl) prayer after performing the 'Asr prayer; however, making up missed (qada') prayers is permissible. 

• Another Group's View: It is impermissible to perform supererogatory prayers (nawafil) after 'Asr, but permissible to make up missed prayers or other nonobligatory prayers performed for a particular reason, such as funeral prayer, tahiyyat al-masjid, or tahiyyat al-wudu' (two rak'ats after ablution).

f: What are the two kinds of conflicting narrations regarding the Prophet ﷺ performing two rak'ats after 'Asr?
b:
1. Narrations portraying the Messenger ﷺ performing two rak'ats after 'Asr only once (implying he never did so again). 

2. Narrations indicating that the Messenger ﷺ performed these two rak'ats on a regular basis.

f: What do the narrations of 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, Umm Salama, and Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (reports 1–3) state regarding why the Prophet ﷺ performed the two rak'ats after 'Asr?
b:
• 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا & Umm Salama رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا: The Prophet ﷺ missed the two rak'ats before 'Asr (or before Zuhr, as clarified in other reports), so after finishing 'Asr, he made them up and never performed them again at that time (Mu'jam al-Tabarani, Musnad Ahmad). 

• Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:45): The Messenger ﷺ performed two rak'ats after 'Asr because some items of charity had arrived, occupying him from performing the two rak'ats of sunna after Zuhr; so he made them up after 'Asr, then did not do so again.

f: How do narrations from 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا and Abu Salama (reports 4–6) describe the regularity of the two rak'ats after 'Asr (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim)?
b:
• 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا: The Messenger would never visit her during the day after 'Asr except that he would perform two rak'ats (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:83) and never neglected them while in her company (Sahih Muslim 1:277). 

• Abu Salama (from 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا): He would perform them before 'Asr, but once missed them due to being occupied with charity, so he performed them after 'Asr; and because whenever he would perform any new prayer [once], he would continue to perform it regularly thereafter, he maintained them (Sahih Muslim 1:277).

f: How does Hafiz Ibn Hajar attempt to resolve the apparent conflict between the affirmative (muthbit) narrations of 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا and the negative (manfi) narrations of Umm Salama رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا?
b:
• Applying the principle of hadith (usul al-hadith) that an affirmative (muthbit) text takes precedence over a negative (manfi) one, Hafiz Ibn Hajar concluded that 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا affirmative narrations hold more strength. 

• He reasoned that 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا reporting was based on her personal knowledge of the Prophet's ﷺ regular actions in her company, while Umm Salama's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا negation was based on her own observation.

f: What does 'Allama Taqi 'Uthmani (Darse Tirmidhi 1:427–428) point out regarding the narration in Sahih Muslim that refines Hafiz Ibn Hajar's explanation?
b:
• A narration in Sahih Muslim reveals that 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا knowledge of this prayer was actually acquired from Umm Salama رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا (i.e., Umm Salama رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا was the original source). 

• The incident initially took place in Umm Salama's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا company when the Prophet ﷺ made up the missed Zuhr sunna after 'Asr. 

• Afterwards, because of the Prophet's ﷺ habit of maintaining any practice he began once, he continued to perform them in 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا company on a daily basis, while Umm Salama رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا remained unaware of this ongoing practice—explaining why 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا affirmed it while Umm Salama رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا negated it.

f: What is the final ruling and view of the Hanafi school and other scholars regarding performing nonobligatory prayers after 'Asr for the Umma?
b:
• One Group: Claims it is sunna to perform the two rak'ats after 'Asr for others as well, citing 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narrations. 

• Hanafi Scholars and Others: State that these two rak'ats cannot be considered a general sunna based on these narrations alone, as they were specific to the Prophet ﷺ making up his missed Zuhr sunna. Consequently, it is prohibitively disliked (makruh tahrimi) for anyone else to perform any nonobligatory prayer at that time, given the numerous other prohibitions.

f: How do 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narration (Sunan Abi Dawud 1:182) and Umm Salama's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا response illustrate that the two rak'ats after 'Asr were an exclusive practice (khasa'is) of the Prophet ﷺ?
b:
• 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narration: The Messenger ﷺ would perform prayer after 'Asr but would prohibit others from it, just as he would fast continuously (yuwasilu) but prohibit others from doing so. 

• Umm Salama's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا response: When Umm Salama رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا observed him performing the two rak'ats and asked if she could make them up if missed, he said no (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:306). 

• Scholarly consensus: Al-Khattabi and Ibn al-Uqayli stated that this prayer is among the unique practices (khasa'is) of the Messenger ﷺ and was not legislated as being sunna for the rest of the Umma.

f: What explicit prohibitions against praying after 'Asr are narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Amr ibn 'Abasa, and Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا?
b:
• Abu Sa'id al-Khudri رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:82–83): "There is no [supererogatory] prayer following Fajr until the sun rises, nor after 'Asr until the sun sets". 

• 'Amr ibn 'Abasa (Sahih Muslim): "Perform the Fajr prayer; thereafter, abstain from any prayer while the sun is rising until it has fully risen. And perform the 'Asr prayer; thereafter, abstain from any prayer until the sun sets". 

• Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Sunan al-Nasa'i 96): Prohibited prayer after 'Asr.

f: How did prominent Companions like 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ enforce the prohibition against performing prayers after 'Asr?
b:
• 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: When Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ performed two rak'ats after 'Asr on the way to Makka, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ called for him and expressed anger, saying: "By Allah, you are aware that the Messenger ﷺ has prohibited us from performing them" (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:303). 

• Enforcement: 'Sa'ib ibn Yazid and Jabala ibn Suhaym narrated that they saw 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ beating Munkadir (or beating a person) for performing prayer after 'Asr until the person terminated his prayer (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:304). 

• Abdullah ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: Stated, "Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ disliked the performance of prayer after 'Asr, and I dislike what Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ dislikes" (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:304).

f: What is the final conclusion of the chapter regarding supererogatory prayers after 'Asr?
b:
• The conflict between single-occurrence narrations (making up missed Zuhr sunna) and regular practice narrations is resolved by recognizing it as an exclusive practice (khasa'is) and unique habit of the Messenger ﷺ to continue any new prayer he initiated. 

• In light of weighty evidence explicitly prohibiting prayer after 'Asr and the actions of the Companions, Hanafis conclude that the strongest and most correct view is that supererogatory prayers after 'Asr are prohibited, and narrations indicating permissibility only illustrate actions exclusive to the Prophet ﷺ.

f: What are the five times designated by Islamic law as undesirable (makruh) for performing prayers?
b: (1) After the Fajr prayer until sunrise; (2) after the 'Asr prayer until sunset; (3) from the beginning of sunrise until the sun is a spear's length above the horizon; (4) from the time the sun is at its highest point in the sky until it moves on (istiwa'); and (5) from when the sun turns yellow before sunset until after it has set.

f: What is the Hanafi ruling regarding performing tahiyyat al-masjid when entering the masjid while the Friday sermon (khutba) is in progress?
b: According to the Hanafis and many others, it is not allowed for a person to perform tahiyyat al-masjid upon entering the masjid while the sermon is in progress, because the Messenger ﷺ forbade any form of prayer or conversation during the Friday sermon.

f: How do the Qur'an and hadiths support the obligation of silence and listening during the Friday sermon?
b:
• Qur'an (7:204): "So when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent, that you may receive mercy"—applied by scholars to the sermon as well, requiring silence and attentive listening. 

• Hadiths from Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Sahih Muslim): The Prophet ﷺ stated that whoever says "Remain silent" to their companion while the imam is delivering the sermon has nullified their reward. Since merely telling someone else to keep quiet is prohibited, performing a supererogatory (nafl) action like tahiyyat al-masjid must also be disallowed. 

• Abdullah ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Majma' al-zawa'id 2:184): The Prophet ﷺ said, "When one of you enters the masjid to find the imam on the pulpit [delivering the sermon], then no prayer or conversation [is permitted] until the imam finishes".

f: What do the narrations from Salman al-Farsi, Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud) state regarding behavior when the imam appears for the Friday sermon?
b:
• Salman al-Farsi (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:122, Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:369): Whoever performs ritual bath (ghusl) on Friday, applies oil/scent, goes to the masjid, performs as much prayer as ordained, and then maintains silence while the imam speaks, will have all sins from the present Friday to the next forgiven.

• Abu Hurayra رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ / Abu Sa'id al-Khudri رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: Mentions performing what has been ordained, and then observing silence / listening attentively until the imam finishes his sermon.

• Nubaysha al-Hudhali (Musnad Ahmad): If he finds the imam present, he sits silently and listens attentively until the imam completes the Friday prayer.

f: What reports from Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, Uqba ibn 'Amir, Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, and others establish the stance against praying once the sermon begins?
b:
• Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا & Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:124): Disliked any prayer or conversation on Friday once the imam had appeared to deliver the sermon.

• Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: Would remain in prayer on Friday, but when the imam would appear, he would stop praying.

• Uqba ibn 'Amir (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:370): Prayer while the imam is on the pulpit (minbar) is disobedience (ma'siya).

• Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Abu Qilaba, Abu Malik al-Qurazi, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Mujahid: Stated that a person entering the masjid while the imam is delivering the sermon should sit down and not engage in any prayer.

f: How do scholars (including Imam Nawawi, Allama Shawkani, and Ibn Abi Shayba) document the practice of the early generations regarding prayer during the Friday sermon?
b:
• Imam Nawawi (Sharh Sahih Muslim 1:288): States that no prayer during the sermon was the established practice of 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, and 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

• Allama Shawkani: Notes that great hadith master Zayn al-Din 'Iraqi related the same practice from Muhammad ibn Sirin, Qadi Shurayh, Ibrahim al-Nakh'ay رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Qatada, and Zuhri.

• Ibn Abi Shayba: Reported this opinion from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, 'Ata', and 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr.

f: How do Hanafis address the narration of Jabir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sahih Muslim 1:287) where the Prophet ﷺ ordered Sulayk al-Ghatafani to stand and perform two rak'ats while the sermon was in progress?
b:
• This cannot stand as evidence for prayer being permissible during the sermon because it speaks of a lone and isolated incident (it was ordered only once).

• In contrast, numerous narrations state that the Prophet ﷺ ordered people to sit down during the sermon.

f: How do other incidents (such as the desert Arab complaining about drought/floods, a person hurrying over people's shoulders, Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ entering, and 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ arriving when 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was delivering the sermon) support the prohibition of praying during the Friday sermon?
b:
• Desert Arab (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:137, Sahih Muslim 1:280): Arrived during the sermon twice to speak to the Prophet ﷺ about rain/floods, and in another incident was admonished for not performing ghusl, but was never commanded to perform any prayer. 

• Person hurrying over shoulders (Sunan al-Nasa'i 207, Abi Dawud): Told to sit down quickly because he inconvenienced people, without being ordered to pray. 

• Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sunan Abi Dawud 156): Told to "Come forth, O 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud" and sit when he sat by the door, rather than being told to pray. 

• 'Uthman's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ arrival: 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ admonished him for arriving late but did not order him to pray. 

• These incidents instruct sitting down while the imam delivers the sermon, proving that the command to Sulayk was due to another reason.

f: What are the various scholarly explanations used to address and reconcile the incident of Sulayk al-Ghatafani (Sahih Muslim 1:287) with the prohibition of prayer during the sermon?
b:
(a) Special circumstance / poverty: The Prophet ﷺ ordered Sulayk to stand and pray so his poverty-stricken and shabby state (worn clothing) would become visible and known to the Companions so they could contribute to him with open hearts; thus it was a unique circumstance and not a general rule. 

(b) Before the sermon began: The Prophet ﷺ was sitting on the pulpit waiting to begin or had not yet stood up/commenced the sermon (noted by Imam Nasa'i in his chapter "Prayer Before the Sermon"). 

(c) Interrupted sermon / silent waiting: The Prophet ﷺ interrupted his sermon or remained silent until Sulayk finished, so Sulayk was not engaged in prayer while the active sermon was ongoing.

(d) Prerequisite of tahiyyat al-masjid: Sulayk had already sat down upon arrival before praying, and when asked, was told to stand up and perform them so the greeting of the masjid was fulfilled properly.

f: What is the final conclusion regarding performing tahiyyat al-masjid during the Friday sermon?
b:
• It is difficult to claim that tahiyyat al-masjid is permitted at the time of the sermon based on Sulayk's incident, as it was a unique and isolated occurrence.

• In light of clear narrations and the practice of the early generations, performing supererogatory prayers or tahiyyat al-masjid while the Friday sermon is in progress is impermissible.

f: What are the key methodological reasons (usul al-hadith) why the Hanafi position prohibiting prayer during the Friday sermon is considered stronger than the permissive narration?
b:
• Prohibitive Precedence: A hadith prohibiting an action is considered superior to a conflicting hadith that permits it. 

• Qur'anic Harmony: Prohibitive narrations are in harmony with Qur'anic verses forbidding anything that distracts a person from listening to the sermon. 

• Companion & Follower Practice: The prohibitive view is substantiated by the practice of many Companions and Followers, whereas the opposing view rests primarily on the lone narration of Sulayk. 

• Precaution (Ihtiyat): Acting on prohibitions carries greater caution since tahiyyat al-masjid is non-obligatory (leaving it does not incur sin, whereas praying while believing it prohibited violates a prohibition).

f: What is the final conclusion regarding performing tahiyyat al-masjid once the Friday sermon has begun?
b: It is prohibited to perform two rak'ats of tahiyyat al-masjid after the imam has started his sermon.

f: What has been the historical consensus and practice regarding the number of rak'ats in tarawih for the first twelve hundred and fifty years of Islam?
b:
• For about 1,250 years until the 20th century, there was little controversy and a general consensus among Muslim scholars that tarawih is no less than twenty rak'ats (and some held it was more). 

• The practice of the Companions (sahaba), Followers (tabi'in), and subsequent scholars has always been performing twenty rak'ats. 

• A consensus (ijma') was reached among the Companions at the time of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ that tarawih was twenty rak'ats, appointing Ubay ibn Ka'b ؓ to lead the people in twenty rak'ats without any refutation from the Companions or wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

f: What are the views of the four prominent imams (Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Malik) regarding the number of rak'ats in tarawih?
b:
• Imam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Imam Shafi'i, and Imam Ahmad: Unanimous that twenty rak'ats are to be performed during tarawih in Ramadan. 

• Imam Malik: Different opinions are recorded from him—twenty rak'ats, thirty-six rak'ats, thirty-eight rak'ats, or forty-one rak'ats. His more popular view of thirty-six rak'ats is explained by the practice of the people of Madina performing an extra four rak'ats of nafl after every tarwiha (set of four rak'ats) in place of the tawaf performed by the people of Makkah; thus, the actual tarawih component was still twenty rak'ats.

f: What do reports from Nafi' and Imam Shafi'i regarding Makkah and Madina reveal about the historical practice of tarawih?
b:
• Nafi' (Fath al-Bari 4:254 U): Stated, "I never found any one performing less than thirty-nine rak'ats (three of which were witr)"—meaning thirty-six rak'ats total observed in Madina (twenty rak'ats tarawih and sixteen supererogatory nafl rak'ats). 

• Imam Shafi'i: Observed people performing thirty-nine rak'ats in Madina (including three witr) and twenty-three rak'ats in Makkah. 

• Ibn 'Abd al-Barr noted that twenty rak'ats was the opinion followed by the majority of scholars, including Kufa, Imam Shafi'i, and most other jurists.

f: What do prominent scholars (such as Ibn Taymiya, Allama Subki, Allama Suyuti, Allama Shawkani, and Mawlana Wahid al-Zaman) state regarding the existence of authentic and direct narrations from the Prophet ﷺ concerning a fixed number of rak'ats for tarawih?
b:
• Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiya: Whoever assumes there is a fixed number of rak'ats reported from the Messenger ﷺ concerning tarawih, and does not accept any greater or lesser number, has erred (Majmu' al-fatawa 46 U, Mirqat al-mafatih 3:381). 

• Allama Subki: It has not been narrated as to how many rak'ats the Messenger ﷺ performed during those nights in congregation, whether twenty or less (Tuhfat al-akhyar 116 U). 

• Allama Suyuti: Scholars have differed on the number of rak'ats; if it had been established through the practice of the Messenger ﷺ, they would not have differed regarding it (al-Masabih 42 U). 

• Allama Shawkani: To confine the prayer known as tarawih to a stipulated number of rak'ats is not understood from the Sunna (Nayl al-awtar 3:53 U). 

• Mawlana Wahid al-Zaman: There is no fixed number for the prayer in the nights of Ramadan, i.e., tarawih (Nazl al-abrar 1:126 U).

f: Why are there no authentic and direct reports from the Prophet ﷺ concerning the exact number of rak'ats in tarawih?
b: The Messenger ﷺ performed the prayer in congregation for a few days only, after which he performed tarawih in the confines of his home for fear of it turning into an obligation (fard) on the Umma. Hence, many Companions did not observe him performing it, and the prayer continued to be performed individually or in small groups until the time of 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.

f: How do scholars use the weak narration of Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (stating the Prophet ﷺ performed twenty rak'ats) and the scholarly consensus (ijma') established by 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ?
b:
• Although classified as weak, the narration of Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا can be used as evidence because it is supported by the consensus of Companions and the practice of the whole Umma generation after generation for over 1,250 years. 

• Furthermore, even if Ibn 'Abbas's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا narration is rejected, the consensus (ijma') reached by 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ—establishing twenty rak'ats—would be sufficient evidence, as 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ stipulation of twenty rak'ats could only have been acquired from the Messenger ﷺ himself (since prayer numbers cannot be determined through personal preference and went unopposed by any Companion).

f: What is the significance of the hadith instructing Muslims to "Keep to my Sunna and the Sunna of the guided Khaliphs" (Sunan Abi Dawud, Tirmidhi, Ibn Maja) regarding 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ decision on tarawih?
b:
• The Prophet ﷺ explicitly instructed holding fast to the Sunna of the rightly guided Caliphs (al-khulafa' al-rashidin), meaning they must be followed in their rulings just as the Messenger ﷺ is followed. 

• 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, as the second rightly guided Caliph, put forth the verdict that tarawih be performed as twenty rak'ats, which the Companions unanimously agreed upon without objection. Therefore, his decision must be accepted as if it had come from the Messenger ﷺ himself.

f: How does 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd al-Qari describe 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ congregation and his famous statement regarding it (Sahih al-Bukhari, Muwatta Imam Malik)?
b:
• 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ went out to the masjid during Ramadan and found people scattered in separate groups or praying alone, and remarked: "If I could have them all congregate behind one imam, it would be better." He made a firm commitment and had them all pray behind Ubay ibn Ka'b ؓ. 

• When he went out another night and saw everyone united in congregation, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ remarked: "How great an innovation this is" (ni'mat al-bid'atu hadhihi, i.e., a practice that has been revived).

f: How do scholars (such as Allama Tibi in Fath al-Mulhim) interpret and explain 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ statement referring to tarawih congregation as a "wonderful innovation" (ni'mat al-bid'atu hadhihi)?
b:
• 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was referring to the praiseworthy deed of encouraging the prayer and reestablishing the congregation after it had not been observed during the caliphate of Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (though observed briefly in the Prophet's ﷺ time before he discontinued it out of fear it would become obligatory). 

• 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ established this procedure as a sunna for time to come (sunna mu'akkada, not a fard), earning the reward of this tradition and all who observe it until the Day of Judgment.

f: How do hadith scholars respond to the fact that Yazid ibn Ruman's narration (Sunan al-Bayhaqi, Muwatta Imam Malik) reporting twenty-three rak'ats during 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ time is mursal (has a broken chain)?
b:
• Consensus on mursal: By consensus of the hadith scholars, mursal narrations can be used as evidence. 

• Malik's mursal status: It is a narration by Imam Malik, and his mursal narrations in Al-Muwatta rank alongside his mawsul narrations (unbroken chains). 

• Supporting chains: There are many other mursal and mawsul narrations that strengthen it. 

• Shah Waliullah / Imam Shafi'i: Shafi'i stated that the most authentic book after the Qur'an is Al-Muwatta, and all its mursal narrations reach the Prophet ﷺ in some way or another. (Note: The twenty-three rak'ats include twenty tarawih plus three witr).

f: What do the reports from Yazid ibn Khusayfa, Yahya ibn Sa'id, 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi', 'Ata', and Abu Khusayb (Sunan al-Bayhaqi, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba) establish regarding the practice during the caliphates of 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ and 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ?
b:
• Yazid ibn Khusayfa: People performed twenty rak'ats tarawih during 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ time (reciting chapters of a hundred or so verses) and leaned on their staffs from standing for so long during 'Uthman's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ time. 

• Yahya ibn Sa'id / 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi': 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ appointed an imam to lead them in twenty rak'ats, and Ubay ibn Ka'b led congregation in twenty rak'ats tarawih followed by three rak'ats witr in Madina. 

• 'Ata' & Abu Khusayb: Observed people performing twenty-three rak'ats (twenty tarawih + three witr) and Suwayd ibn Ghafala leading five tarwihas (twenty rak'ats in all).

f: How do reports from Shutayr ibn Shakl (from 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ), Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and A'mash (from Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ) corroborate the twenty-rak'a count?
b:
• Shutayr ibn Shakl: 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ led them during Ramadan in twenty rak'ats tarawih and three rak'ats witr (Sunan al-Bayhaqi 4:496). 

• Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: People performed twenty rak'ats in the month of Ramadan during 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ caliphate, lengthening recitation. 

• A'mash: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud would perform twenty rak'ats tarawih and three rak'ats witr (Qiyam al-layl 91 U).

f: What does Imam Tirmidhi's report on the historical dispute over rak'at numbers reveal about the presence of an eight-rak'a opinion in early generations?
b: • The knowledgeable people disputed over numbers (some saying 41 including witr in Madina, majority saying 20), but there is not even a mention of tarawih being eight rak'ats, not even as a weak opinion.

f: What do prominent scholars (such as Ibn Qudama, Imam Nawawi, Hafiz Ibn Hajar, Ibn Taymiya, Imam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, Imam Ghazali, Sayyid 'Abd al-Qadir Jilani, and Shaykh Mansur ibn Idris al-Hanbali) state concerning twenty rak'ats of tarawih?
b:
• Ibn Qudama: 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ appointed an imam to lead people in twenty rak'ats tarawih during Ramadan (al-Mughni). 

• Imam Nawawi: The number of rak'ats in tarawih remained twenty, constantly accepted century after century (Kitab al-Adhkar 83). 

• Hafiz Ibn Hajar: The Companions reached a unanimous verdict that tarawih was twenty rak'ats (Mirqat al-mafatih 3:382). 

• Ibn Taymiya: Twenty rak'ats is the opinion most Muslims follow. Furthermore, Ubay ibn Ka'b led twenty rak'ats amidst the Emigrants and Helpers, and none refuted him (Fatawa Ibn Taymiya 23:112). 

• Imam Abu Yusuf رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (via Asad ibn 'Amr): Informed Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ that tarawih is an emphasized sunna established by 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ based on evidence or information he possessed from the Messenger ﷺ, not through his own preference (I'la' al-sunan 46). 

• Imam Ghazali: Tarawih is twenty rak'ats and is an emphasized sunna (Ihya' 'ulum al-din 1:139). 

• Sayyid 'Abd al-Qadir Jilani: Tarawih is a sunna of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and is twenty rak'ats (Ghunyat al-talibin 567). 

• Shaykh Mansur ibn Idris al-Hanbali: Tarawih is twenty rak'ats during Ramadan.

f: How do scholars address the fact that prayer numbers cannot be determined through human reasoning alone, and why is 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ establishment of twenty rak'ats accepted?
b:
• The number of rak'ats for any prayer cannot be made up or established through one's own intellect and reasoning; it must come from Allah and His Messenger ﷺ. 

• Since all Companions are considered trustworthy ('udul) and would not introduce a concept contrary to the Shari'a, 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ decision of twenty rak'ats—which went completely unrefuted by any Companion or the Prophet's ﷺ wives—indicates it was acquired directly from the Messenger ﷺ.

f: How do scholars answer those who use 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا narration about eleven rak'ats (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:154) to claim that tarawih consists of only eight rak'ats?
b:
• It is tahajjud, not tarawih: Abu Salama's inquiry to 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا was regarding whether the Prophet ﷺ performed any extra rak'ats of tahajjud during Ramadan. 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا stated he would perform no more than eight rak'ats (tahajjud) throughout the year, regardless of the month. 

• Practiced year-round: 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا explicitly noted this prayer was performed both in and out of Ramadan ("neither in Ramadan nor out of it"), whereas tarawih is exclusively a Ramadan prayer. Other narrations confirm the Prophet ﷺ increased his worship specifically during Ramadan.

f: How do hadith compilers (such as al-Marwazi, Imam Muslim, Nasa'i, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Ibn Maja, Ibn Khuzayma, and Imam Malik) treat Abu Salama's narration from 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا (Sahih al-Bukhari) regarding the 11 rak'ats?
b:
• Categorization in Collections: None of these major hadith compilers included Abu Salama's hadith in their chapters on tarawih, despite it being a sahih narration in Sahih al-Bukhari. 

• Categorized under Tahajjud or Witr: Instead, they included this narration exclusively in their chapters on tahajjud or witr. Had it been regarding tarawih, they would have surely placed it in their tarawih chapters. 

• 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا Acceptance of Consensus: Furthermore, if the hadith had concerned tarawih, 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا would have rejected or corrected the consensus (ijma') established by 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ for twenty rak'ats. Thus, the prayer she described was none other than tahajjud.

f: How do scholars criticize and contextualize the narration of Jabir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sahih Ibn Hibban, Ibn Khuzayma) which states that the Prophet ﷺ performed eight rak'ats in Ramadan?
b:
• Weak Narrator ('Isa ibn Jariya): The sole narrator reporting this from Jabir رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ is 'Isa ibn Jariya عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, who has been heavily criticized and declared weak/unreliable by Yahya ibn Ma'in ("he is not strong"), Imam Nasa'i, Abu Dawud, 'Uqayli, Saji, and Ibn 'Adi. Severe criticism takes precedence, rendering the chain weak and unacceptable as evidence. 

• Single Night vs. Multiple Nights: The detailed report in Qiyam al-layl (p. 91) shows this occurred for only one night in congregation, and mentions fear of witr becoming obligatory rather than tarawih, causing Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani to hesitate in equating it to 'Aisha's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا general narrations (Fath al-Bari 2:12 U). 

• Does Not Negate Home Performance: Even if accepted, it only records the number of rak'ats performed in congregation before retiring home, and does not negate that the Prophet ﷺ completed the remaining twelve rak'ats at home.

f: How do scholars critique the narration of Sa'ib ibn Yazid in Muwatta Imam Malik (1:71) stating 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ appointed imams to lead people in eleven rak'ats?
b:
• Inconsistency Across Chains (Idtirab): Five different reports transmit this from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, and all five contradict each other: 

1. Imam Malik's version: Mentions 11 rak'ats, but does not mention Ramadan. 

2. Yahya ibn Qattan's version: Mentions 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ brought people behind Tamim al-Dari ؓ for 11 rak'ats, without mentioning a specific command or Ramadan. 

3. 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad's version: Mentions 11 rak'ats during 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ caliphate, omitting specific commands, Ubay ibn Ka'b ؓ, Tamim al-Dari ؓ, or Ramadan. 

4. Ibn Ishaq's report: Mentions they performed 13 rak'ats in Ramadan during 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ period. 

5. 'Abd al-Razzaq's version: Describes 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ explicitly commanding that twenty-one rak'ats (20 tarawih + 1 witr) be performed instead of eleven. 

• Evaluation by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr: The great Maliki jurist Ibn 'Abd al-Barr gave preference to the narration of twenty-one rak'ats and explicitly labeled the narrations mentioning eleven as an "erroneous assumption" (wahm) (Rak'ate tarawih 39).

f: Why is the narration of Sa'ib ibn Yazid ؓ transmitted through Yazid ibn Khusayfa preferred over the version transmitted through Muhammad ibn Yusuf?
b:
• Consistency and Authenticity: All versions of Sa'ib ibn Yazid's narration related via Yazid ibn Khusayfa (through students Ibn Abi Dhi'b and Muhammad ibn Ja'far) are unanimous in specifying twenty rak'ats. Imam Nawawi, Iraqi, Suyuti, and others judged these chains (asnad) as strong and reliable. 

• Methodological Preference: Justice in hadith analysis demands accepting the consistent, rigorously authenticated narration of Yazid ibn Khusayfa over the confusing and contradictory versions transmitted through Muhammad ibn Yusuf.

f: How do Imam Bayhaqi and Ibn Habib al-Maliki reconcile the eleven-rak'a and twenty-rak'a narrations regarding 'Umar's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ caliphate?
b:
• Imam Bayhaqi (Sunan al-kubra 2:496): Explains that the Companions initially performed eleven rak'ats in congregation, after which they transitioned to performing twenty rak'ats and three witr. 

• Ibn Habib al-Maliki (Tuhfat al-akhyar 192 U): Clarifies that tarawih was initially performed as eleven rak'ats with prolonged recitation. When this proved difficult for the people, they increased the number of rak'ats to twenty (excluding witr) and shortened the recitation in each rak'a to ease the difficulty.

f: What is the final scholarly conclusion regarding the established sunna amount for tarawih prayer?
b:
• The view that tarawih consists of only eight rak'ats is a recent opinion unsupported by any masjid congregation or pious predecessor (salaf salihin) throughout the first twelve hundred-plus years of Islam. 

• Since there is unanimous agreement among the four Imams and the overwhelming majority of scholars across Islamic history, twenty rak'ats is conclusively established as the sunna amount.

f: How do the Hanafi school and other scholars explain the hadiths stating that the Prophet ﷺ combined two obligatory prayers while traveling?
b:
• Hanafi Explanation (Jam' al-suri / "Apparent Combining"): Although the Prophet ﷺ performed the prayers one after another, he actually performed each prayer in its own proper time. For example, when combining Maghrib and 'Isha, he would stop a short time prior to the end of Maghrib and perform it, then as soon as the time of 'Isha entered, he would perform 'Isha. 

• Other Scholars (Jam' al-haqiqi / "Real Combining"): They explain that the Messenger ﷺ performed both Maghrib and 'Isha together within the time of 'Isha (i.e., after Maghrib had expired).

f: What are the definitions of jam' al-suri, jam' al-haqiqi, jam' al-taqdim, and jam' al-ta'khir?
b:
• Jam' al-suri ("Apparent Combining"): Performing the first prayer toward the end of its time and the second prayer immediately after, at the beginning of its time. 

• Jam' al-haqiqi ("Real Combining"): Performing two obligatory (fard) prayers within a single prayer time. 

• Jam' al-taqdim ("Advanced Combining"): Performing Maghrib and 'Isha in the time of Maghrib, or Zuhr and 'Asr in the time of Zuhr (performing one prayer before its time). 

• Jam' al-ta'khir ("Delayed Combining"): Combining prayers at the time of the later prayer because one of the prayers is delayed from its specific time.

f: What is the view of Imam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ regarding when jam' al-haqiqi (real combining) is permissible?
b:
• According to Imam Abu Hanifa رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, jam' al-haqiqi is not permissible except at 'Arafat (during Hajj), where advanced combining takes place between Zuhr and 'Asr, and at Muzdalifa, where pilgrims perform delayed combining between Maghrib and 'Isha. 

• The practice of combining at these two places is established through scholarly consensus; outside of these two instances, Hanafis interpret all hadiths on combining as referring to jam' al-suri.

f: How do Qur'anic verses (such as 4:103, 2:238, 107:5, and 19:59) support the Hanafi stance on performing prayers at their fixed, stipulated hours?
b:
• Qur'an 4:103: "Verily the prayer is enjoined on the believers at fixed hours [times]"—meaning every prayer has an appointed time prior to which it is invalid and after which it becomes qada' (missed), indicating the importance of performing each prayer in its own time. 

• Qur'an 2:238: "Guard strictly the [five obligatory] prayers". 

• Qur'an 107:5 & 19:59: Mentioning woe to those who are negligent in regard to their prayer / gave up prayers, which scholars explain as an admonition for those who delay prayers beyond their stipulated times.

f: How do key hadiths from Abu Musa رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud establish that combining two prayers out of their fixed times is impermissible (kaba'ir)?
b:
• Abu Musa al-Ash'ari رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:459): The Messenger ﷺ said: "Combining two prayers together without any valid reason is from the major sins (kaba'ir)". 

• 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (al-Ta'liq al-sabih 2:124): Wrote to people prohibiting them from combining two prayers together, informing them that doing so was a major sin. 

• Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (Sahih al-Bukhari 1:227, Sahih Muslim 1:417): Stated: "I never observed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform any prayer out of its time except at Muzdalifa," where he combined Maghrib and 'Isha.

f: How do narrations from Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا, and Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا explicitly describe the mechanics of jam' al-suri ("apparent combining")?
b:
• Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shayba 2:458): Clarifies that the Prophet ﷺ combined Maghrib and 'Isha while on a journey by delaying Maghrib until just before its expiry time and performing 'Isha immediately as its time entered. 

• 'Aisha رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا (Sharh Ma'ani 'l-athar 1:164): Narrated that while on a journey, the Prophet ﷺ would delay Zuhr and perform 'Asr early, and delay Maghrib and perform 'Isha early (i.e., each prayer in its own time). 

• Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Sahih Muslim 1:246): Abu 'l-Sha'tha explained Ibn 'Abbas's رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا narration by stating that the Prophet ﷺ delayed Zuhr to the end of its time and performed 'Asr as soon as it entered, and likewise delayed Maghrib and performed 'Isha early. 

• Ibn 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا (Sunan Abi Dawud 1:178): When the red twilight (shafaq ahmar) nearly disappeared, he performed Maghrib, then waited until the red had completely disappeared and performed 'Isha, noting that the Prophet ﷺ did this when in a hurry.

f: How does 'Allama 'Ayni ('Umdat al-qari 3:568) reconcile narrations mentioning the disappearance of red twilight (shafaq) with the Hanafi position on prayer times?
b:
• There are two types of shafaq (twilight): the redness (ahmar) after sunset, and the whiteness (abyad) remaining shortly after the redness disappears. 

• According to the view that Maghrib time ends when white twilight disappears, if the Prophet ﷺ performed Maghrib immediately after red twilight disappeared, he performed it during the whiteness (within its stipulated time). 

• Concurrently, under the view that 'Isha time begins when red twilight disappears, 'Isha was also performed within its proper time, fully confirming jam' al-suri.

f: How does the narration of Mu'adh رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1:124, Sunan Abi Dawud 1:178) regarding the Expedition of Tabuk describe the method of combining prayers, and what criticisms/reconciliations apply to it?
b:
• Description of Jam' al-Suri: It specifies that if setting out before noon, he delayed Zuhr to perform it [just prior to its expiry time] with 'Asr, and if departing after noon, he performed 'Asr early with Zuhr [Zuhr at the end of its time and 'Asr as soon as it entered], doing the same for Maghrib and 'Isha in their respective times. 

• Rejection by Imam Abu Dawud: 'Allama 'Ayni noted that this narration was rejected by Imam Abu Dawud, who stated that there is no clear hadith to be found concerning the performance of a prayer before its stipulated time. 

• Weakness of Narrator (Husayn ibn 'Abdillah): Hadith experts heavily criticized Husayn ibn 'Abdillah in the chain: Ibn al-Madini abandoned his reports, Imam Ahmad stated he has defects, Ibn Ma'in declared him weak (da'if), and Nasa'i stated his narrations are rejected.

f: How do Hanafis explain the narrations in Sahih Muslim (1:246) from Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا stating that the Prophet ﷺ combined prayers in Madina "without fear, rain, or travel"?
b:
• Since fear, rain, and travel are the main three prerequisites under which other scholars permit jam' al-haqiqi, performing real combining without any of these reasons would violate established legal principles. 

• The correct interpretation is that Ibn 'Abbas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا was describing "apparent combining" (jam' al-suri), wherein the Prophet ﷺ delayed the first prayer to the end of its time and offered the second prayer immediately thereafter at the beginning of its time, while remaining in Madina.

f: What is the final conclusion regarding combining two prayers (jam') in Hanafi jurisprudence?
b:
• The Hanafi approach of interpreting combined prayers as "apparent combining" (jam' al-suri) is the safest and most uncontroversial method. It preserves total harmony with Qur'anic verses and hadiths strictly requiring prayers to be performed in their appointed times. 

• Interpreting reports as jam' al-haqiqi creates direct contradictions with established texts. Furthermore, even scholars who permit jam' al-haqiqi agree that it is superior to perform each prayer separately within its own respective time.
